title: Ventura AI POC: traffic surface & sizing kickoff
summary: Kickoff to scope a 2-week POC to validate latency and cost targets for Ventura AIs inference workload. Covered QPS and concurrency patterns, token-length distributions for short chat vs long summarization use cases, benchmark plan (microbench + production shadow), and acceptance criteria (p95 latency and throughput / cost targets). Agreed to share traffic CSV and benchmark template; Redwood to run initial capacity mapping and propose instance/config mix.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet and traffic model template (link) by 2026-06-27
Ventura to provide 7 days of anonymized traffic CSV and top 50 prompt examples by 2026-06-30
Schedule pilot kickoff (run microbench) week of 2026-07-06
SE to propose capacity mapping and expected cost delta by 2026-07-02
action_items: Maya Patel - share benchmark spreadsheet and traffic template - due 2026-06-27
Lena Hu - export anonymized traffic & sample prompts - due 2026-06-30
Ethan Ruiz - initial capacity map + config recommendations - due 2026-07-02
Carlos Mendes - confirm network/VPC constraints and confirm access method (private agent or S3 upload) - due 2026-06-29
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-25 14:00 UTC | Duration: 55 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Ventura Head ML), Carlos (Platform Eng), Priya (Product)
---
Summary (auto): Kickoff for POC to validate throughput and latencies for chat+summarization workloads, agree on success criteria and data sharing.
---
00:00:03 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm maya from Redwood, ae focused on fintech/ai verticals.
00:00:10 Lena: hi all, lena here, head of ML at ventura. we run the customer support and triage models.
00:00:15 Carlos: carlos platform engineering, i'll handle infra bits.
00:00:18 Priya: priya, product, i'll own acceptance criteria from a biz side.
00:00:22 Ethan: and i'm ethan, se at redwood, i'll walk through the workload questions and benchmark plan.
00:00:30 Maya: great. objective today is to align on traffic shape, target slos, what success looks like and timelines for a 2-week pilot. feel free to interrupt.
00:00:45 Lena: perfect. to set context, we have two main flows: quick chat assistant for customers (very short prompts, 10-40 input tokens, 20-70 output tokens typically) and a longform summarization flow for support threads (inputs up to 2k tokens, outputs 400-800 tokens).
00:01:05 Ethan: ok so that's already helpful—so token distribution is bimodal. do you have a sense of QPS on these?
00:01:16 Lena: production average qps about 8 during day, peaks at 45 for chat during marketing pushes, summaries are lower qps ~0.5 to 1 but heavy on tokens.
00:01:30 Carlos: and concurrency wise, we see bursts where many small chats come in parallel, so concurrency can hit 150 short requests concurrently in peaks.
00:01:40 Ethan: got it. two patterns: high qps short tokens, low qps high-token long ops. that impacts batching and KV cache needs.
00:01:50 Maya: can you also call out SLA requirements or p95 latency targets?
00:01:55 Priya: for the chat assistant we want p95 < 250ms ideally, p99 < 400ms. for summaries we accept higher, p95 < 2s, p99 < 4s. cost per 1k tokens also matters.
00:02:10 Ethan: important to know. just to level-set—p95 numbers under 250ms for short responses are aggressive but doable with the right model/quantization and serving pattern; may require dedicated capacity or low-latency hosted tier.
00:02:24 Lena: we're open to dedicated if it keeps latency consistent. security wise we need VPC connectivity and KMS for keys, plus SOC2 docs.
00:02:35 Maya: we'll include SOC2 and the private deployment checklist in the doc bundle.
00:02:40 Ethan: quick question about traffic history—do you have sample distributions? not raw PII but a CSV with timestamp, request type, input_token_count, output_token_count, response_time, success flag is perfect.
00:02:55 Lena: yes we can provide 7 days with anonymized ids. we'll remove user ids and anything sensitive.
00:03:05 Carlos: note our network restricts egress to certain IP ranges; if you need private agent we'll need to coordinate.
00:03:12 Ethan: noted, we'll propose both S3 upload and private agent options.
00:03:20 ---
00:03:30 Maya: let's talk benchmarks. proposal: phase 1 microbenching - run per-model latency QPS matrix with representative input lengths; phase 2 shadow piloting - mirror a small percentage of production traffic for 48 hours; phase 3 acceptance tests on p95/p99 and cost calculations.
00:03:50 Priya: sounds good. how long does microbench take?
00:03:54 Ethan: depends on model variants and sequence lengths. each model-length cell 10k tokens of sampling is typical, we can get initial results in 48-72 hours once traffic template and weights are set.
00:04:10 Maya: what about concurrency modeling—how do you map bursts to machines?
00:04:15 Ethan: we use a concurrency distribution and a token-per-request histogram to build a queuing model—key knobs are batch size, preferred latency SLO, kv cache hit rate. if chat is mostly short with high qps, small batch/low-latency configs are best; long summaries benefit from batching and async pools.
00:04:35 Lena: can you simulate our exact burst patterns? we have sudden spikes 0->45 qps in under 3 minutes.
00:04:42 Ethan: yes, we can replay a timestamped trace in the benchmark harness; that will show queuing and whether fallback routing triggers.
00:04:50 Carlos: fallback routing?
00:04:52 Ethan: yeah, policy we propose: primary route to low-latency model; if capacity saturated fall back to quantized variant or to a slightly cheaper model with similar quality. we'll show expected quality deltas in the bench.
00:05:05 Priya: ok, product cares about quality. we need automatic regression alerts if answers degrade.
00:05:10 Maya: Redwood Optimize can hook evals to prompt sets and trigger alerts; we'll include that in the handoff.
00:05:18 ---
00:05:30 Ethan: i want to call out token skew—in your chat flow, what fraction of chats include context history? that increases input token size.
00:05:36 Lena: roughly 30% include 2-3 turns history, pushing inputs from 20 tokens to 100 on avg.
00:05:44 Ethan: ok that increases effective cost and latency. please mark that in the CSV.
00:05:50 Carlos: for the private deployment, are there example network diagrams we should review?
00:05:55 Maya: yes, we'll share our private deployment diagram and the VPC peering checklist in the benchmark bundle.
00:06:02 ---
00:06:15 Maya: let's put concrete success criteria on the table. Priya: product acceptance for chat: p95 <= 250ms for 95% of peak windows, error rate < 0.5%, cost per 1M tokens under $X (we'll draft numbers). For summary flow: p95 <= 2s, p99 <= 4s, completeness/ROUGE threshold for summaries.
00:06:40 Priya: yes, and we want a pass/fail matrix per test.
00:06:45 Ethan: we'll produce a test matrix and a binder of benchmark scripts. for ROUGE/QA checks we'll run a small eval on top 50 prompts you provide.
00:06:55 Lena: timeline check: we can get traffic CSV and prompts by 6/30. we want pilot started early july.
00:07:02 Maya: redwood to run microbench and share results by 7/2 or 7/3. then shadow pilot week of 7/6.
00:07:10 Carlos: engineering bandwidth is limited week of 7/6, we may need the shadow to be light (1-2% traffic).
00:07:16 Ethan: that's fine, we'll start at 0.5-1% and ramp if things look good.
00:07:22 ---
00:07:35 Priya: what about cost modeling? can you provide best/worst case cost estimates based on qps/concurrency?
00:07:41 Ethan: yes i'll produce a cost table: per 1k token cost at different batch sizes and expected monthly spend using your traffic profile; that'll be part of the deliverables.
00:07:50 Maya: i'll add that as an action item for ethan.
00:07:54 Ethan: noted.
00:08:00 ---
00:08:12 Lena: small note—our compliance team will ask about key management, audit logs retention for 12 months.
00:08:18 Maya: redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logs; i'll include retention options and the SOC2 artifacts.
00:08:24 Carlos: and SSO, provisioning for SAML?
00:08:28 Maya: yes, SSO and RBAC support.
00:08:31 ---
00:08:45 Maya: last thing, any blockers?
00:08:48 Carlos: only the network egress and our approvals for external pilot. we'll send the internal approval timeline by 6/29.
00:08:55 Lena: none from ml side.
00:08:58 Priya: none.
00:09:00 Maya: great. recap of next steps: maya share benchmark spreadsheet, ethan produce capacity map and cost table, ventura share traces and prompts. schedule pilot kickoff week of july 6.
00:09:15 Maya: i'll send calendar invite for a 30 minute checkpoint after microbench results.
00:09:20 Ethan: and i'll attach the benchmark harness repo link in the follow up.
00:09:28 ---
00:09:40 End of recorded portion; remainder of meeting had ad-hoc infra Q&A not fully transcribed due to overlap.

Notes: referenced artifacts will be shared: benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/links/ventura-bench), traffic template (CSV example), private deployment diagram. Transcription may mis-hear technical terms ("K V cash" instead of KV cache, some proper names).
